# Modeling the Cost of Home Insurance

## High-level Considerations

- Pure Premium vs. Frequency / Severity
- By-peril vs. All Perils
- Modeling & Holdout Data Sets

::: {.notes}

Variables predictive for one peril may not be predictive for others

You need good peril classification of data

Storms can cause multiple claims, leading to correlations across policies in the data set

:::

## Models May Vary by State

- State Statutes may influence territory boundaries:
  - Minnesota Statute 72A.20 Subd. 13
- Some state regulators don't like specific variables
- Some regulatory institutions require revealing more information about your model
- Data availability
  - Some of the data sets aren't available in Alaska and/or Hawaii
  - The data is available, but different
- Cost/benefit for some regions, like Alaska
  - Alaska is huge and requires a ton of processing power
  - Alaska wraps around to the Eastern Hemisphere, so extra edge cases

## Implementation Considerations

:::{.incremental}

- Territory Tables are pre-scored and static
  - Feature engineering is computationally expensive
- The more complicated they get, the harder the implementation gets
- May need to update the filing for re-scoring
- Model version used based on policy effective date
- Make sure your territory assignments match your territories

:::

::: {.notes}
Implementation is hard, and insurance company IT teams often have difficulty implementing rating correctly without having to deal with geospatial data
:::
